name: Hair weave

card.summary: Human or synthetic hair wefts attached to natural hair by sewing, bonding or clips to add length, volume or a different style.
card.note: Tight installation and adhesives are linked to traction alopecia, scalp injury and allergic reactions in case reports.

quick.overview:
A hair weave attaches wefts of human or synthetic hair to a person's own hair to add length, volume or a new style. The look changes immediately and can be kept for weeks.

Weaves are one form of artificial hair integration, alongside clip-ins, braids and wigs. Human hair is the most common choice and synthetic fibres such as Kanekalon are cheaper but less durable.
quick.how: In the track-and-sew method, natural hair is braided into cornrow tracks and wefts are sewn on with a needle and thread. In bonding, wefts are glued on, kept off the scalp. Clip-ins and bulk attachments are alternatives. An invisible-part sew-in takes about an hour and lasts about eight weeks.
quick.risks: Tight braiding or prolonged wear can cause traction alopecia and breakage. Case reports describe full-thickness scalp necrosis after tight braiding and weave placement, and an anaphylactic reaction to latex-containing hair glue. Patch-testing adhesives is commonly advised.

lead: A hair weave, also called hair extensions or artificial hair integrations, adds human or synthetic hair to natural hair to increase length or volume or change style [3]. Wigs are related and also covered under the topic [3].

Methods include track-and-sew, where wefts are sewn onto braided cornrow tracks; bonding with glue; and clip-in or bulk attachments [3]. Wigs were fashionable in the late 17th century, while weaves appeared in the 1950s among celebrities and spread widely in the 1970s [3].
Published research consists mainly of case reports on complications: scalp injury from tight braiding with weave, and latex allergy to hair glue [1][2].

chain: Length, volume or colour changes immediately
A different hairstyle without waiting for growth
angle.text: A weave changes hair length, fullness and style right away, and can be kept for weeks.

infobox: About an hour; lasts about eight weeks

paras: Track-and-sew uses a blunt needle and thread matched to hair colour; bonded wefts are glued and are often patch-tested first [3]. Human hair is the most common material, with 'tangle-free' hair chemically treated; synthetic fibres such as Kanekalon and Futura are cheaper but wear faster and are damaged by heat [3].
Tight braiding or long wear is associated with traction alopecia, breakage and follicle damage; glue has been linked to dermatitis and sensitivity [3].

A 2015 case report describes extensive full-thickness scalp loss in a young woman after tight spiral braiding and weave, needing complex reconstruction [1]. Another 2015 report describes a 29-year-old woman with airway-compromising angioedema after latex-containing hair glue was applied for a weave; glue was removed over hours with an oil-based conditioner [2].
No studies found beyond case reports of complications [1][2].
